## Test Image Analysis

**Key visual features observed:**
- **Single, isolated oval/elliptical lesion** on an otherwise healthy dark green banana leaf
- **Very dark (near-black) center** — the necrotic core
- **Orange-brown halo/zone** surrounding the dark center, creating a classic "bullseye" or "eye-spot" appearance
- **Lesion is ~2-3 cm in size**, well-defined edges
- No streaking, no yellowing of the overall leaf, no vein discoloration

## Disease Reasoning

| Disease | Match? | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| **Cordana_Leaf_Spot** | ✅ Strong | Classic oval lesion, dark center, orange-brown halo — textbook eye-spot pattern |
| Anthracnose | Partial | Dark lesions possible, but typically sunken/fruit-focused |
| Yellow/Black Sigatoka | Low | Usually streaks or multiple lesions, not isolated bullseye |
| Panama_Disease | No | Causes leaf yellowing/wilting, not focal spots |
| Bunchy_Top | No | Vein streaking, bunched leaves — completely different |
| Cigar_End_Rot | No | Affects fruit tips only |

The isolated "eye-spot" lesion with a dark center and warm orange-brown halo is the hallmark presentation of **Cordana Leaf Spot** (caused by *Cordana musae*), which forms characteristic oval spots on banana leaves.
